content:
The image shows a mango leaf with scattered small dark/black spots across the surface. The spots appear as small, discrete dark flecks distributed over a yellowing-green leaf. There is no white powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew), no thick black sooty encrustation covering the surface (rules out Sooty Mould as a primary diagnosis), and no gum secretion or bark discoloration (rules out Die Back).

The small dark spots are consistent with early Anthracnose lesions — irregular dark spots on the leaf surface. The leaf also shows some yellowing and the spots match the description of irregular, oval-shaped spots distributed across the leaf surface. The spots are small, dark, and sunken-looking rather than raised, which aligns with anthracnose rather than bacterial canker.

However, looking more carefully, the dark specks are very small and scattered uniformly, which could also suggest early Sooty Mould colonies. But the spots appear more discrete and lesion-like rather than a continuous black coating, pointing more toward Anthracnose.

The overall pattern — discrete dark spots on a yellowing leaf with no powdery white coating and no continuous black film — best matches Anthracnose.
